working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass, and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is home to arguably the world's greatest links course in Royal County Down, but many UK visitors don't realise there are two or three other genuinely compelling courses nearby that reward building a short circuit rather than a single-destination trip. The post treats the county as a coherent golf region, covering what each course actually demands of a visitor (booking logistics, cost reality, character) rather than simply restating rankings.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD) Championship Links, Newcastle, County Down. Par 71. Consistently ranked No.1 in the world by Golf Digest and Golf Monthly's UK & Ireland Top 100. Set in Murlough Nature Reserve between the Mourne Mountains and Dundrum Bay. Opened 1889. Designed with input from Old Tom Morris, Harry Vardon, Harry Colt among others.
- RCD visitor green fees 2026: Championship Links £450 (20 April–16 October 2026); Annesley Links £120 same period. 2027 fees already published at £495 / £150.
- RCD visitor days: Championship Links = Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun. Annesley Links = Mon, Thu, Fri, Sun. Wednesday and Saturday are NOT visitor days.
- Booking: no ballot. Visitors submit an enquiry form via the club website; Reservations Team responds with availability. Tee-time availability is 'exceptionally limited' (club's own language). All play in four-ball groups; minimum one caddie required per group. Forecaddie costs £110 per group. Full payment in GBP at time of booking; non-refundable.
- RCD dress code: collared shirts required; no blue denim, cargo shorts, tracksuits, leggings. Soft-spiked shoes strongly advised. Hats/caps off indoors.
- Annesley Links (No.2 course): par 66, 4,940 yards from men's tees. Good fallback if Championship is unavailable or budget is a factor; described as more manageable in wind.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, Ardglass village, County Down. Founded 1896. Par 70, 6,268 yards (white tees). Clubhouse partly occupies a fortified building with origins dating to 1405 (one of the oldest buildings used as a golf clubhouse in the world). Irish Sea comes into play on eight holes. Open to visitors every day. Approximately 30 minutes from RCD, around an hour from Belfast. Green fees range broadly by season (sources show seasonal variation from c.£90 low season to c.£220+ high season — do not state a single definitive current figure; direct the reader to check with the club). Par 70.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links, Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, County Down. Founded 1902; course shaped by James Braid (visited 1934). Par 70 (some sources say 69), c.6,167 yards. Most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland. Nearest links to Belfast (~45 min). Quick-draining links terrain; rarely closed after rain. Visitors welcome every day. Green fees notably lower than RCD or Ardglass (Golfshake guide cites from £35 midweek / £40 weekend — treat as indicative only; direct reader to check current rates). Recognised for value. Signature challenge: par-4 10th at 435 yards, cited as one of the hardest par-4s in Irish golf.
- Kilkeel Golf Club: 12 miles from RCD, served as qualifying venue for British Amateur and Senior British Open. Worth noting as an additional option for a longer stay.
- Warrenpoint Golf Club: established 1893, parkland, within Hall Estate in shadow of Narrow Water Castle. One of top parkland courses in Northern Ireland.
- Getting there: Belfast has two airports — George Best Belfast City (BHD, 30–40 min to Newcastle by car) and Belfast International (BFS, ~1hr 15min). Ferries to Belfast from Cairnryan (Scotland) and Liverpool. Newcastle is ~45 min from Belfast via the A24. County Down courses use GBP (not euros).
- Accommodation: Slieve Donard Resort (Marine & Lawn), Newcastle — directly adjacent to RCD, 4-star. Burrendale Hotel also in Newcastle, ~1 mile from RCD. Newcastle is described as a pleasant seaside town and practical base.
- Note on RCD blind shots: several tee shots are blind; a local caddie or printed course guide is genuinely useful, not just a luxury.
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate or state a single definitive current green fee for Ardglass or Kirkistown as a precise figure — sources show seasonal variation and some data is dated; describe in general terms or direct reader to check directly with clubs.
- Do not invent quotes attributed to any golfer, pro, or reviewer.
- No invented personal anecdotes about playing any of these courses.
- No affiliate links unless the accommodation or operator appears in the approved-partners list; mention any hotel or tour operator informationally only if not pre-approved, with no link and no note to the reader about why.
- No gambling or betting content.
- No specific medical/injury advice beyond generic warm-up guidance.
- No financial advice on whether the trip represents value or is affordable for a given reader.
- Northern Ireland uses GBP, not euros — do not conflate with Republic of Ireland pricing.
- Do not duplicate coverage of Royal Portrush or the Antrim/Causeway Coast, which is a different region; keep focus on County Down specifically.
- Avoid duplicating the angle of any Wales, Scotland or English coastal circuit posts already published — this post covers Northern Ireland, a region not yet covered in the existing slugs.
